original_value: Convolution neural network (CNN) is an efficient technique to detect objects in various kinds of images, especially for microaneurysm (MA) of diabetic retinopathy in retinal fundus image. This study proposes a deconvolutional neural network to accurately discriminate MA from non‐MA. The deconvolution, instead of pooling operation, is embedded into the CNN to recover the erased details of feature maps of convolutional layers. Three types of images are collected for training and predicting. Furthermore, the extracted features are fed into the fully‐connected layers to classify using a softmax layer. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve significant sensitivity and accuracy on multiple public datasets, in comparison to the state‐of‐the‐art. For Retinopathy Online Challenge dataset, the sensitivity and accuracy are improved up to 0.798 and 0.986, respectively.

result.paraphrase: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are an efficient way to detect objects in many image types, particularly microaneurysms (MAs) associated with diabetic retinopathy in retinal fundus images. This study introduces a deconvolutional neural network designed to distinguish MA from non-MA with high accuracy. Instead of pooling, deconvolution is incorporated into the CNN to restore feature-map details lost in convolutional layers. Three image types are gathered for training and prediction. The extracted features are then passed to fully connected layers and classified with a softmax layer. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves notable sensitivity and accuracy on several public datasets compared with state-of-the-art approaches. On the Retinopathy Online Challenge dataset, sensitivity and accuracy reach 0.798 and 0.986, respectively.
